title: The Life of a Star
blurb: One number — mass at birth — decides brightness, colour, lifespan and how it dies. Run a star from molecular cloud to remnant on a live HR diagram.

sources.cite: Duric, N. — Advanced Astrophysics, Cambridge University Press, 2004
Ekström et al. 2012, A&A 537, A146 (Z=0.014, non-rotating)
sources.note: Interpolated from evolutionary models. The textbook t = 10 Gyr·M/L shortcut underestimates massive stars by ~4x because their convective cores mix far more hydrogen into the burning region.

sources.claim: initial–final mass relation for white dwarfs
sources.note: Calibrated for 0.83 < M_i < 7.2; clamped below that so a remnant can never exceed its progenitor.

sources.cite: Jeans 1902, Phil. Trans. R. Soc. A 199, 1

open: The upper mass boundary between neutron-star and black-hole formation is uncertain and metallicity-dependent; 20 M_sun is a convention, not a measurement.
Mass loss through stellar winds is not modelled, which matters most above ~30 M_sun.
